course_name_original: Estructuras Metálicas, de Hormigón y Cimentaciones
prerequisites: Having completed the courses: Elasticity and Strength of Materials I, Elasticity and Strength of Materials II, and Calculation and Design of Structures.
It is desirable to know the contents and calculation procedures seen in the courses Elasticity and Strength of Materials I and II and Calculation and Design of Structures.
It is recommended to take the course Analytical Mechanics and Methods of Structural Analysis to complete students' knowledge regarding Structures.

Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Be able to know and analyze the technical characteristics of reinforced concrete in relation to the structural elements in which it participates. Know the related materials for their correct planning and execution on site.
Be able to analyze the mandatory regulations for the development of metallic and reinforced concrete structures, both for foundations and for building and retaining structures.

Be able to analyze and know the different types of steel and existing soils, emphasizing their technical characteristics related to the execution of the structure. Knowledge of existing test types and compliance with mandatory regulations depending on the soil category and building typology.

Be able to analyze the types of foundations and metallic profiles available and the ideal choice of type to use depending on soil conditions and building conditions. General knowledge of the main advantages and disadvantages of the main types and superficial knowledge of less conventional systems.

Be able to analyze and apply the content worked on for the specific calculation of a shallow foundation, composed of footings and tie beams, as well as metallic profiles, up to the embodiment of these constructive elements in a technical report and the necessary planimetry for their correct execution.

syllabus_topics: Flexural buckling: Ideal member and Real member
Supports. Simple members and composite members
Bolts: constructive arrangements and local stresses
Execution of welds: types of beads and connections
The portal frame as a substructure. Transverse stiffness. In-plane stiffness. Distribution of actions. Analysis methods. Soil interaction.
Examples of special structures such as Off-Shore Structures will be presented.
Placement of reinforcements. Formwork and molds.
Manufacturing, dosing, and on-site placement. Beam Calculation
Anchor plates. Direct foundations: types of footings. Analysis and dimensioning. Bearing capacity and allowable pressure.
Calculation of a shallow foundation composed of footings and anchor plates. Deep foundations: pile calculation.
teaching_methods: Computer practices (creating calculation programs with Excel, application of structural calculation software, problem-solving, interpretation of results)
Field trips (visit to a metal sector company)
Theoretical-Practical classes (Expository method/master class, flipped classroom, case studies, problem-solving exercises, problem-based learning)

assessment_methods.method: Written assignments and their presentation in class
Report on practical work on structural calculation
Oral presentations of group work analyzing and calculating solutions for specific cases related to metallic structures and foundations
Final face-to-face exam to evaluate overall course learning

assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by written assignments and presentations (30%), a report on practical work (20%), oral presentations of group work (20%), and a final face-to-face exam (30%). The practical work is mandatory. No electronic devices are allowed during exams or classes without express authorization.
